digest.component_or_area: test suite / CLI store read regression
propositions: Fault-seeded matrix (F1-F7) proves the generic property does not subsume the original regression oracle; F3 and F6 (partial-success records) are caught only by test_cli_show_complete_or_erroring_under_write_burst and missed by both generic tests.

Reverting the actual slim-fetch-ledge fix (_RECONVERGE_LOCK_TIMEOUT 2→15) leaves both burst tests green; only the deterministic held-lock tests detect the original regression, proving the named burst test does not protect against its regression.

The two test files are complements rather than duplicates: F5 and F7 are caught only by the generic property while F3 and F6 are caught only by the original, establishing bidirectional non-subsumption.

Measured wall-clock times (macOS 8.17–8.76s, Ubuntu CI 12.79–14.93s) confirm test cost; zero savings are available from consolidation since deletion would forfeit F3/F6 detection, requiring runtime recovery from storm downsizing instead.

By Just et al. FSE 2014 mutation-testing criterion, a test removal is safe only when it does not decrease mutation score; here removal decreases score by losing F3/F6 coverage, licensing retention of both oracles.

Process concurrency (F1 detection requiring 15s stall under live lock) and cleanup (F5 subprocess timeout + thread release) remain observable and real; no serialization or mocking masked the concurrent behavior.
